newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Ousted leader urges Afghans to resist Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Ousted leader urges Afghans to resist Taleban.

text.p: Afghanistan's ousted president, Burhanuddin Rabbani, urged Afghans on Friday to resist the Taleban Islamic militia, hours after it captured the capital Kabul and set up a new government.
A Pakistan-based Afghan news service quoted a statement from Rabbani as asking Afghan party leaders to unite against Taleban and form a "proper government" in the war-battered country.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said the statement, issued from an undisclosed place, was approved by a Rabbani-led council.
It urged the Afghan people to resist the Taleban government and warned Pakistan, which Rabbani had accused of helping the militia, that Taleban would come to a bad end.
The whereabouts of Rabbani, his prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and their government's top military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, were not clear.
Taleban sources in Kabul said Masood retreated to his stronghold of Jabal-ul-Seraj, 70 km (44 miles) north of Kabul, after Taleban fighters took control of the capital.
Afghanistan's ambassador to India, Masood Khalili, told a news conference in New Delhi that Rabbani and members of his government were about 25 km (15 miles) north of Kabul.
